doc.title: Hide Tanaka interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, April 3, 2014

title: Traditional Japanese music and his mother the shamisen player
summary: He describes traditional Japanese instruments (flutes, shamisen, tsuzumi, taiko) and says his mother played shamisen.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: If someone came to your country, an American came to your country and wanted to hear traditional Japanese music, what does that consist of?
Oh like Japanese traditional instrumental. The most popular things are a kind of flute, you know, those woodwinds.
So they cannot play any — like twelve notes. It’s possible but very difficult. And three strings instrument, we call it a shamisen. Like I play it like this. And a tsuzumi, like a
Taiko too. Taiko drums. We don’t have much but instrumental.
And does that kind of music get performed in Japan?
Yeah, yeah, yeah, yeah. Actually my mother was a shamisen player.
Oh. How do you spell that?
S-H-A-M-I-S-E-N. Shamisen. It means three taste strings.
